# Diana Barry

## Overview

- **Age:** 18 years old  <sub>[v2 c29 P24](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0024)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v3 c29 P13](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0013)</sub>
- **Origin:** Orchard Slope  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** Treasurer of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society  <sub>[v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Di  <sub>[v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025)</sub>

## Appearance

Diana is a very pretty girl with black eyes, rosy cheeks, and glossy, jet-black hair. Inheriting her father's merry expression, she is prone to dimpling. As she matures, her figure becomes somewhat plump and rounded.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 c17 P10](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0010), [v2 c17 P4](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0004), [v2 c29 P30](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0030), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Diana is a good, smart, and unselfish friend with a pleasant and comfortable demeanor. She laughs easily and exhibits ladylike behavior, though she takes a very practical view of life. Although lacking the vivid imagination of her closest companion, she possesses a warm, loyal heart and a quiet, supportive nature.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P26](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0026), [v1 c19 P81](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0081), [v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017), [v2 c2 P10](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0010), [v2 c6 P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002), [v3 c12 P59](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0059)_

## History

Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. As a child, she met Anne Shirley and the two swore a solemn, lifelong oath of bosom friendship over imaginary running water. Though briefly separated when her mother forbade their companionship after an accidental intoxication incident, the friendship was restored after Diana sought Anne's assistance during her sister Minnie May's severe attack of croup. Diana actively participated in childhood pastimes, including the Story Club and local performances. When older, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society as its treasurer. She did not pursue higher education at Queen's Academy or Redmond College, remaining in Avonlea while her friends moved away. Diana became engaged to Fred Wright at eighteen, and the two later married at Orchard Slope. Following their wedding, she gave birth to their first child, a son named Fred.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029), [v1 c18 P21](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0021), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P23](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0023), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011), [v2 c29 P24](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0024), [v3 c29 P13](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0013), [v3 c39 P41](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0041), [v3 c39 P44](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0044)_

- Named by a boarding schoolmaster who stayed with her family when she was born  <sub>[v1 c2 P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064)</sub>

## Quotes

> I love you devotedly, Anne, and I always will, you may be sure of that.  <sub>[v1 c17 P9](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0009)</sub>

> Trees haven’t souls, but the smell of dead fir is certainly lovely. I’m going to make a cushion and fill it with fir needles. You’d better make one too, Anne.  <sub>[v2 c6 P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002)</sub>

> I’d wish to be tall and slender.  <sub>[v2 c13 P33](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0033)</sub>

> We are not really parting, Anne. I’m not going far away. We’ll love each other just as much as ever. We’ve always kept that ‘oath’ of friendship we swore long ago, haven’t we?  <sub>[v3 c29 P3](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0003)</sub>

> Before he came I wanted a girl, so that I could call her ANNE. But now that little Fred is here I wouldn’t exchange him for a million girls. He just couldn’t have been anything but his own precious self.  <sub>[v3 c39 P44](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0044)</sub>
